bib.title: Multilingual Denoising Pre-training for Neural Machine Translation

read.skipped: Appendix B translation examples are garbled non-Latin text; not needed

question: Does pre-training a complete sequence-to-sequence model by denoising monolingual text in many languages improve supervised, document-level and unsupervised machine translation?
hypothesis: Multilingual BART-style denoising pre-training of a full seq2seq model gives gains across MT settings and enables transfer to pairs with no bi-text or unseen languages.
contributions: mBART, first method to pre-train a complete seq2seq model by denoising full texts in multiple languages
gains up to 12 BLEU on low-resource MT, over 5 BLEU on many document-level and unsupervised settings
new transfer types: fine-tune on one pair, translate from other pre-training languages; benefit for languages unseen in pre-training
analysis of number of languages, pre-training steps, bi-text size, comparison with back-translation

method.summary: A 12+12 layer Transformer seq2seq is pre-trained on CC25 (25 languages) with BART noising (35% word-span masking, sentence permutation), then fine-tuned per language pair on bi-text (sentence or document level) or used to initialise unsupervised MT.
method.task: multilingual denoising pre-training for machine translation

datasets.name: CC25 (Common Crawl, 25 languages)
datasets.size: En 300.8 GB / 55608M tokens down to My 1.6 GB / 56M tokens (Table 1)
datasets.source: Common Crawl (Wenzek et al. 2019; Conneau et al. 2019)
datasets.preprocessing: re-balanced by up/down-sampling with lambda_i = (1/p_i) * p_i^alpha / sum p_i^alpha, alpha = 0.7; one SentencePiece model learned on full CC data, 250,000 subword tokens; no truecasing or normalisation

datasets.name: 24 bi-text pairs (WMT, IWSLT, FLoRes, IITB, WAT19)
datasets.split: low <1M, medium 1M-10M, high >10M pairs; validation likelihood for selection
datasets.source: WMT16/17/18/19, IWSLT15/17, FLoRes En-Ne/En-Si, IITB En-Hi, WAT19 En-My

datasets.name: WMT19 En-De document
datasets.preprocessing: sentences separated by </S>, instance ends with <LID>; each doc split into 2-4 instances

datasets.name: TED15 Zh-En document
datasets.split: test 2010-2013 TED following Miculicich et al. 2018

models.name: mBART25
models.architecture: Transformer seq2seq, 12 encoder + 12 decoder layers, extra layer-norm on top of encoder and decoder

other.pretrain_langs: Ro, It, Cs, Fr, Es, En

models.name: Random
models.architecture: no pre-training; hyper-parameters (architecture, dropout etc.) grid-searched per task

training.objective: maximise sum log P(X|g(X)); g = mask 35% of words in spans with length ~ Poisson(lambda=3.5) plus sentence permutation; decoder input is original text offset by one, language id token <LID> as first token
training.batch_size: around 128K tokens per GPU as printed (matching BART)
training.dropout: 0.1, reduced to 0.05 at 250K steps and 0 at 400K

other.fine_tuning: 0.3 dropout, 0.2 label smoothing, 2500 warm-up steps, 3e-5 max learning rate, max 40K updates low/medium resource and 100K high resource, model selected by validation likelihood, teacher forcing
other.unsupervised_BT: on-the-fly back-translation; output restricted to target-language tokens (those >=1% in target monolingual corpus) for first 1000 steps

inference.prompting: language id token at encoder and decoder; document decoding stops when <LID> predicted

metrics.name: BLEU
metrics.definition: Papineni et al. 2002, with language-specific tokenisation (Indic-NLP, KyTea Ja, Mecab-Ko, QCRI Ar, Moses Ro, sacreBLEU zh, default otherwise); s-BLEU sentence-level and d-BLEU document-level matching

eval.protocol: single reported scores, no significance tests

availability.code: Fairseq (Ott et al. 2019); no mBART release stated

evidence.quote: The total batch size is around 128K tokens per GPU, matching BART (Lewis et al., 2019) conﬁguration.

results.claim: mBART25 gives large gains over random init on low-resource En-Vi (Vi-En).
mBART02 gets 20.7+ BLEU on En-De with only 10K training pairs while random init scores 0.0.
results.setup: En-De subsampled bi-text, mBART02 vs Random, Fig 4
results.quote: The pre-trained model is able to achieve over 20 BLEU with only 10K training examples,

results.claim: mBART02 achieves the best Ro-En score in the pre-training comparison, above mBART25.
results.setup: WMT16 Ro-En fine-tuning; mBART02 38.5 vs mBART25 37.8 vs Random 34.0

results.claim: mBART25 + BT sets state of the art on Ro-En (mBART02+BT 39.9 vs mBART25+BT 38.8).
Document-level Doc-MT fine-tuned from mBART25 beats Sent-MT on En-De by d-BLEU, while random Doc-MT fails.
results.table: Table 9(a), row Doc-MT, column mBART25 d-BLEU (Random 7.7)

results.claim: Document-level Zh-En d-BLEU with mBART25 Doc-MT versus HAN.
results.table: Table 9(b), row Doc-MT, column mBART25 (HAN 24.0, Random 3.2)

results.claim: Unsupervised BT on dissimilar pair Ne-En: mBART gets 10.0 BLEU where XLM gets 0.5.
results.setup: En-Ne initialised from mBART25, trained on CC25 monolingual data

results.claim: In high-resource settings pre-training does not help and slightly hurts above 25M pairs (Zh-En 33.3 vs random 35.0).
Fine-tuning on one pair transfers: Ko-En-fine-tuned model translates Ja-En etc. without bi-text; e.g. fine-tune Zh then test Ja 9.9 BLEU, random init gives about 0 BLEU.
results.quote: which always ends up with ≈0 BLEU.

results.claim: Pre-training for En-My costs 300~3000 GPU hours vs back-translation pipeline 5+300+350; mBART02 matches BT on En->My (37.8 vs 37.7).
results.setup: My-En using 79M En and 29M My sentences

results.claim: After just 25K steps (5% of training) mBART models outperform the best baseline on Ro-En, and keep improving by over 3 BLEU through 500K steps.
results.setup: Ro-En fine-tuning from checkpoints every 25K steps
results.quote: after just 25K steps (5% of training), both models outperform the best base-

results.claim: Fine-tuning fails at extremely low resource: En-Gu with about 10K pairs gets 0.3 BLEU.

limits: Fails at ~10K pairs (En-Gu) and gives no consistent gain or slightly hurts above 25M pairs (Table 3).
Pre-training on more languages slightly hurts (<1 BLEU) when target monolingual data is plentiful (De, Ro); capacity dilution suspected.
Model is expensive to deploy; authors leave efficient models and mBART100 to future work.
Optimal noising strategy not explored; fine-tuning on unseen source languages is harder, left for future work.
Single runs, no seeds or significance tests; learning rate for pre-training and warmup not given; BT comparison not equal in monolingual data (BT benefits from larger En data).
